scalars.scalar_value: Education, Public Health, Psychology, Counseling, or Social Work) or equivalent combination of education and experience is required.

A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience that includes direct supervision of young adults/student staff in leadership positions; crisis intervention and/or personal support/counseling services for individuals who have experienced sexual violence, dating/domestic violence and/or stalking; leadership of prevention programs/initiatives; and program and event planning.

The regular hours for this full-time position are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday – Friday, except during the designated summer period when office hours end at 4:30 p.m. Overtime, holiday, weekend and evening work hours may be required. Regular hours may vary due to needs of the College or division.

items.item_text: Master’s degree in related field (e.g. Education, Public Health, Psychology, Counseling, or Social Work) or equivalent combination of education and experience is required.

A minimum of 3 years of relevant experience that includes direct supervision of young adults/student staff in leadership positions; crisis intervention and/or personal support/counseling services for individuals who have experienced sexual violence, dating/domestic violence and/or stalking; leadership of prevention programs/initiatives; and program and event planning.
Initiate and plan training and programming for the campus community regarding violence prevention, risk reduction and education strategies.
Prepare and conduct training in the areas of Title IX, Clery, sexual violence, domestic and dating violence, stalking, sexual harassment and discrimination.
Respond to workshop and training requests, utilizing current best-practices.
Develop and lead a comprehensive strategic plan for the prevention of sexual violence, dating/domestic violence, stalking, sexual harassment and discrimination at the College.
Provide direct oversight of and regular supervision, training, support for the CARES Campus Advocates.

Maintain current knowledge of local, state, and federal laws and regulations regarding sexual violence, dating/domestic violence, stalking, sexual harassment and discrimination. Work with the Title IX & Clery teams to assist with policy development, compliance review, assessment and annual reports.
Collaborate with the Office of Communications to create College-wide educational publications (print and web) and marketing campaigns.
Assist with the evaluation and assessment of programs on a regular basis, maintaining records of program effectiveness.

Assists in providing initial care, support and advocacy to those who report incidences of sexual violence, dating/domestic violence, stalking, sexual harassment and/or discrimination. Provides information and referral services to campus and community resources.

Partner with Campus Life and Housing and Residence Life to communicate compliance and violence prevention to all incoming students (First Year, Transfer, and International) through orientation programs and information distribution.
Ensure that compliance records regarding prevention education and support services are accurate and kept current.
Administer, manage and monitor programming & training budgets for peer programs.

Collaborate with new and existing campus partners, e.g., Project Sister Family Services, EmPOWER Center, Housing and Residence Life, Queer Resources Center, Monsour Counseling and Psychological Services, and other Consortium partners.
Other projects and duties assigned by the Title IX Coordinator/Clery Officer and Associate Dean.
